## a3342a9df65d

**Reproduced lesson-identifiability defect.** Assigned generator SHA-256:
`9a30db2f04606cc53434cd3a1c67cc922aae8390d8f4136100a4536e33321e42`;
executed rule hash: `773f3bdd64c2`.

For seed `39`, difficulty `medium`, samples `0,1,2` as demonstrations and sample
`3` as query, the selected rule sorts components by size descending and breaks
equal-size ties by color ascending. A rival that breaks ties by color descending
matches all three demonstrations exactly because they contain no equal-size
components. The query contains color-5 and color-9 components of size 3; the
rival then disagrees with the authoritative Racket output by 9 cells. All four
inputs pass the target's `self_check()`, so they belong to its generated domain.

The complete source-bound witness—including grids, component sizes, rival
outputs, canonical output hashes, seed/sample policy, validation findings, and
command—is `checks/audit/a3342a9df65d/surviving-rival.json`. Authoritative Racket
application evidence is `checks/audit/a3342a9df65d/racket.json`, with inputs in
`checks/audit/a3342a9df65d/input.json` and generation provenance in
`checks/audit/a3342a9df65d/generation.json`.

The audit also found that lint fails because `RULE_HASH` is missing and advertised
singleton enum axes are not probeable (`checks/audit/a3342a9df65d/lint/result.json`).
The semantic stage reports no executable contract rather than proving
identifiability (`checks/audit/a3342a9df65d/semantic/result.json`). This target
was audit-only and was not modified.
